historical_references.reference: Motasim Billah (r. 242-247 AH/856-861 CE) was the eldest son of the Abbasid caliph, Al-Mutasim Bi-llah. He assumed the throne upon his father's death at the age of 25. During his rule, Motasim was faced with several rebellions and invasions, including the revolt of Barmakids and the invasion of the Mongols. He was able to put down the rebellions but was ultimately defeated by the Mongols at the Battle of Dabik (863 CE). Motasim died during the retreat and was succeeded by his brother, Al-Mu'tamid.

Motasim bin Abdullah (d. 335/947) was a prominent scholar, poet, and philosopher of the Abbasid period. He was born in Baghdad, Iraq, and studied under the famous scholar, al-Kindi. Motasim wrote extensively on philosophy and logic, and his most famous work, 'The Discourse on the Sovereignty of Reason', is considered a seminal text in the history of Islamic philosophy. He was also known for his contributions to the field of mathematics and astronomy.
